- issues opened in `experiment-repo`#2 ("Result files in a fixed schema for Fig 2-6 and Tables 1-3") by `figtab-repo`  > # Request: result files in a fixed schema so the figures and tables can be generated from them
  > 
  > **Purpose.** Fig 2–6 and Tables 1–3 of the Outline are generated by scripts in `figtab-repo` directly from your result files; I never retype a number. **Waits on this:** every real exhibit. The generators and a schema validator are being written now against this schema, so please emit it (or tell me what to change in my reader instead — one reply is enough).
  > 
  > **Format.** Tidy CSV (or parquet), one row per (cell × method), committed in `experiment-repo` under `results/` (large raw per-rep output may stay out of git; the aggregated files below are what I read). UTF-8, one header row, `NA` for not-applicable.
  > 
  > ## `results/cells.csv` (E1, E3, E4, E5, E6, E7 — all aggregated cells)
  > | column | meaning |
  > |---|---|
  > | `exp` | E1…E8 |
  > | `dataset` | ppi-python set name, or synthetic scenario id (`syn_affine`, `syn_gauss`, `syn_sigmoid`, `syn_nonmono`, `syn_mcar_viol`, …) |
  > | `n`, `N` | labeled / unlabeled sizes used in the cell |
  > | `tier` | `T1` (f only) or `T2` (f and X) |
  > | `method` | stable id: `labels_z`, `labels_wilson`, `labels_cp`, `ppi`, `ppipp`, `pooled_linear`, `strat_ppi`, `calib_iso`, `calib_spline`, `calib_bins`, `ppipp_on_calib`, `vec_ppipp_x`, `ols_adj`, `gbm_aipw`, `floor` (+ any others, with a one-line description in `results/METHODS.md`) |
  > | `construction` | `wald`, `wilson`, `boot_t`, `t`, `conc` … |
  > | `reps` | Monte-Carlo repetitions behind the row |
  > | `truth` | the target value used (pool mean) |
  > | `coverage`, `cov_lo`, `cov_hi` | empirical coverage with its Wilson 95% interval |
  > | `width_mean`, `width_se` | mean interval width and its MC standard error |
  > | `ratio_vs_ppipp`, `ratio_lo`, `ratio_hi` | **paired** (same draws) mean width ratio to PPI++ with CI, same `construction` family stated in `ratio_ref` |
  > | `bias`, `bias_se` | mean(estimate − truth) with MC SE |
  > | `valid` | `1/0` per the Brief's win rule (coverage not significantly below nominal and not below PPI++ beyond MC error); `valid_reason` when 0 |
  > | `sampling` | `with_replacement` / `disjoint` / `labeled_only_resample` (ballots) / `shift` (plankton) |
  > | `seed`, `commit` | base seed and code commit that produced the row |
  > 
  > ## `results/prop_check.csv` (E1/E2, Fig 2)
  > `dataset`(scenario), `n`, `N`, `calibrator`, `pred_excess_var`, `meas_excess_var`, `meas_excess_var_lo`, `meas_excess_var_hi`, `pred_excess_width`, `meas_excess_width`, `…_lo`, `…_hi`, `delta` (Δ), `sigma2_res`, `reps`. Excess is over the floor V* for PPI++ and for each calibrator (long format, `estimator` column).
  > 
  > ## `results/breakeven.csv` (E4, Fig 4)
  > `dataset`, `calibrator`, `d_eff`, `K`, `n`, `N`, `ratio_vs_ppipp`, `ratio_lo`, `ratio_hi`, `pred_nstar`, `pred_nstar_lo`, `pred_nstar_hi`, `meas_nstar` (NA if not crossed in the grid).
  > 
  > ## `results/diagnostic.csv` (E4/E8, Fig 5)
  > Per (dataset × n × calibrator): `delta_hat`, `learning_cost`, `headroom_hat` (= Δ̂ − cost), `headroom_hat_lo/hi`, `realised_gain` (1 − width ratio vs PPI++), `gain_lo/hi`.
  > 
  > ## `results/ladder.csv` (E3, Fig 3)
  > Can be derived from `cells.csv`; if you prefer to emit it, one row per (dataset, n, step) with `step` ∈ {`classical`, `ppi`, `ppipp`, `calib_T1`, `calib_T2`, `floor`} and the SE-factor / construction-factor split as separate columns (`se_ratio`, `constr_ratio`).
  > 
  > ## Also, with each file
  > - A `results/README.md` line per file: what it was computed on (data, n/N grid, reps, sampling scheme, seeds) — it goes into captions.
  > - Failed / not-run cells listed explicitly (rows with `reps=0` and a reason), so an empty place in a figure is never mistaken for a pass.
  > - The script that wrote each file, so my `FIGURES.md` chain is script → file → script → figure.
  > 
  > If you can only supply part first, E1 (`prop_check.csv`) and the n-sweep rows are the most useful to me early: they are Fig 2 and Fig 4, the figures that carry C1 and C3.
